profile.headline: Software Engineer at VueMed
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
Languages and technologies: Java, Spring, Angular, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, C# | Google Apigee, AWS Cloud, Firestore, Git, Postman, Splunk, Jira

Gaming and I have a very close relationship; I started playing games when I was two years old and competed in multiplayer games when I was five. Growing up playing competitive games, I thought about how to leverage my computer game resources to accomplish sub-goals and eventually victory. Action games forced me to think quickly, while puzzle and strategy games developed my creative thinking. Regardless of the genre, all games emphasized problem-solving.

Naturally, I quickly picked up on the problem-solving aspects of software engineering. As a student at Stuyvesant High School and Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, I considered the various quirks of my assignments and the tradeoffs between solutions. I focused on developing software in the most efficient and readable manner, much like I conceived strategies with minimal losses in my video games.

Working as a software engineer consultant at Capgemini, I was whisked from one project to another. My ease of adaptability allowed me to quickly pick up tech stacks I had never encountered before, from front-end technologies like Angular and TypeScript to cloud platforms such as AWS Cloud and Google Apigee. Leveraging my creative thinking and ability to work with new rules and situations, I swiftly contributed to various teams, delivering impactful results in a short time.

Today, I utilize my eclectic working experience and passion for problem-solving to tackle challenges from diverse perspectives. My rich background equips me with the tools to deconstruct even the most complex problems into manageable chunks. In the future, I aspire to grow my skill set by learning various methods and coding principles to develop efficient applications. By taking on larger and tougher challenges, I seek to advance my career as an independent contributor.
